dispatch: DA 279; REV 203's two findings, both verified by driving before any change
THE_LESSON_WORTH_A_LINE: A LEDGER ROW CAN BE WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND BOTH HAPPENED AT ONCE. My ledger read 5/6 and REV's read 5/6 on DIFFERENT rows, and both of mine were wrong. A property list that omits a property makes a gate look satisfied for exactly the reason it is not.

CORRECTION_1_A_FALSE_NEGATIVE_FROM_MY_OW.truth: the properties were intact; the PROBE was broken
CORRECTION_1_A_FALSE_NEGATIVE_FROM_MY_OW.cause: the probe passed a BARE LIST as the canonical population. REVIEW 202's provenance rule correctly refuses one, because a population with no provenance cannot be told from one fabricated around the rows under test.
CORRECTION_1_A_FALSE_NEGATIVE_FROM_MY_OW.measured_before_the_fix: every gate-4 property cell returned REFUSED CANONICAL_POPULATION_HAS_NO_PROVENANCE
CORRECTION_1_A_FALSE_NEGATIVE_FROM_MY_OW.measured_after: one clean row -> OK n_actions=1 folded=1; two sides -> OK n_actions=1 folded=2; duplicate key -> REFUSED FORECAST_ACTION_DUPLICATE_KEY; claimed-on-path vs population -> REFUSED FLAG_CONTRADICTS; off-population -> counted as ACTION_NOT_IN_THE_CANONICAL_POPULATION
CORRECTION_1_A_FALSE_NEGATIVE_FROM_MY_OW.this_is_the_third_of_its_shape: after the cwd bug (every count 0) and the guessed step-4 paths (NO_FILES_ON_ANY_EXECUTING_REF while two files sat on both refs). A false negative manufactured by the instrument reads exactly like a finding.

CORRECTION_2_A_FALSE_POSITIVE_FROM_AN_IN.truth: UNSATISFIED -- the ninth property was never written down
CORRECTION_2_A_FALSE_POSITIVE_FROM_AN_IN.the_missing_property: both arms replay on the same ACTION POPULATION
CORRECTION_2_A_FALSE_POSITIVE_FROM_AN_IN.cause: identical in shape to the price_path hole REVIEW 201 found: an input that lives OUTSIDE ReplayInputs is an input the comparison cannot see. run_arm(actions, value_of, inputs) takes the action list as an ARGUMENT, so compare_arms never sees it.
CORRECTION_2_A_FALSE_POSITIVE_FROM_AN_IN.measured: two arms replaying 6 actions and 3 actions are reported inputs_identical=true with an IDENTICAL inputs_digest, baseline n_quotes=6 and challenger n_quotes=3, no refusal. A challenger that drops half the population passes the seam.
CORRECTION_2_A_FALSE_POSITIVE_FROM_AN_IN.reverts_to_satisfied_when: `action_keys_sha256` becomes required (no default) or is COMPUTED inside run_arm from the actions it was handed, so the protection does not depend on a caller opting into it. That is what made the price_path fix structural.
CORRECTION_2_A_FALSE_POSITIVE_FROM_AN_IN.AND_THE_GATE_MOVED_WHILE_I_WROTE_THIS: Q-DE-370 landed at 486867e between my commit and my push, making the action list a FIELD of ReplayInputs. Re-driven at the new parent rather than left standing: the row is STILL unsatisfied, but for a NARROWER and more precise reason than my first property name implied, so the property was split into four.
CORRECTION_2_A_FALSE_POSITIVE_FROM_AN_IN.WHAT_REMAINS: the guard is OPT-IN where the tape guard is MANDATORY. `action_keys_sha256` defaults to "" and the check reads `if inputs.action_keys_sha256`, so a caller that omits the field is never checked at all. `price_path` has NO default and cannot be omitted. Driven: two arms on 6 and 3 actions with the field omitted compare inputs_identical=true, no refusal, quotes 6 vs 3.

WHAT_THIS_CHANGES_ABOUT_READING_THE_LEDG: a green row is only as strong as the property list it was scored against, and that list is MY enumeration rather than the plan's. `properties.n_declared` is carried for exactly that reason: it is a claim about how many properties I wrote down, never a claim that they are all of them. A reader comparing two seats' counts must compare the LISTS, not the numbers -- which is how REV found this and how the §11-versus-§5 keying error was found one dispatch earlier.

THE_INSTRUMENT.measured_now: gates_satisfied 5/6 at 486867e; gate 6 is the single unsatisfied row, 10 of 12 properties
THE_INSTRUMENT.no_labelled_score_permitted: TRUE again (5 < 6), having been FALSE while gate 6 read satisfied on an incomplete list

UNCHANGED_FROM_V5: keyed on §5's SIX BUILD GATES, with the §11 step as a separate column and the divergence at 6 stated
every status COMPUTED at verification time: presence by count at a fetched ref, behaviour DRIVEN in a worktree cut at that ref, properties driven against the same bytes
score_is_evidence_permitted additionally requires §11 step 6's full-pipeline freeze, which does not exist on either executing ref (measured: 0)
STEP_6_FREEZE_DRAFT: DA 278's draft remains UNLANDED and is not affected by this correction. It reads six of six from REV only, never from this ledger, and its own `ready_to_land` requires an empty gap list AND that return; it currently carries 15 blocking gaps.
rule_10: every number and boolean above was computed or driven at the artifact before being written here; this file declares the RULE and the corrections, never a row status.
A_THIRD_THING_THIS_ROUND_TAUGHT: a row can be wrong in both directions AND the ground can move under the row while it is being written. The defence is the same in all three cases: re-drive at the ref before the claim lands, and never let a commit message describe bytes that no longer exist.
